beginner.summary: No database experience assumed. Participants learn relational concepts and write SQL to query, filter, sort, join, aggregate and change data, mainly on PostgreSQL with notes on MySQL and SQL Server differences, and finish by answering business questions on a sales database.
prerequisites: Comfortable using a computer and spreadsheets
Can install software or use a provided lab environment
outcomes: Write SELECT queries with filters, sorting, joins and aggregates
Insert, update and delete data safely

days.topic: Relational Database Concepts and SQL Setup
subtopics: What a database is and why not a spreadsheet
SQL and the main database products
Installing PostgreSQL or using the lab server
days.lab_task: Connect to PostgreSQL with DBeaver and psql, load the sample sales database, draw its tables and relationships, and run five first queries that list rows from each main table.
days.deliverable: Diagram of the sample database and the five queries with results
checks: Identify the foreign key from orders to customers
Correct column named on the diagram
Run the same query in psql

days.topic: SELECT Basics: Columns, Aliases and Expressions
subtopics: Differences between PostgreSQL, MySQL and SQL Server
days.lab_task: Write ten queries on the products and customers tables that select named columns, compute prices with tax, build full names, list distinct countries and show the first ten rows.
days.deliverable: Ten queries with results

subtopics: IS NULL and IS NOT NULL
days.lab_task: Answer fifteen questions by filtering orders, products and customers, such as orders above 500 in March from India or Brazil and customers with no phone number.
days.deliverable: Fifteen queries with results
checks: Find orders between 1 and 31 March over 500
Find customers with no phone number using = NULL and IS NULL
= NULL returns nothing, IS NULL returns 9 rows
Find products whose name contains "pro" in any case

subtopics: ORDER BY one and several columns
days.lab_task: Write queries for a product listing page sorted by price then name, page through results 20 at a time, and find the top five most expensive products per the whole catalogue.
days.deliverable: Sorting and paging queries with results
checks: Sort by price descending then name
Get page 3 with 20 rows per page
Sort a column containing NULLs with NULLS LAST

days.topic: Built-in Functions for Text, Numbers and Dates
days.lab_task: Clean a customer list by trimming and standardising names and emails, compute customer age from birth date, and report order counts by month using date functions.
days.deliverable: Cleaning and reporting queries with results
checks: All lower case with no spaces
Group orders by month with DATE_TRUNC

days.topic: Conditional Logic with CASE and NULL Functions
subtopics: CASE inside SELECT, WHERE and ORDER BY
days.lab_task: Label orders as small, medium or large, replace missing phone numbers with "not given", compute discount rates without division by zero, and sort orders with urgent ones first.
days.deliverable: Queries with results
checks: Count orders in each size band
Divide by a zero quantity using NULLIF
Returns NULL instead of an error

subtopics: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX
GROUP BY one and several columns
days.lab_task: Produce a sales summary showing revenue, order count and average order value per country and per month, and list only countries with more than 50 orders.
days.deliverable: Summary queries and results
checks: Filter groups with HAVING count over 50
Select a column not in GROUP BY

subtopics: Why data is split across tables
days.lab_task: Join orders, order lines, products and customers to produce invoice lines with customer name and product name, and total revenue per product category.
days.deliverable: Join queries and results
checks: Five lines with correct names and totals
Write a join without aliases on an ambiguous column
Error explained and fixed with aliases

days.topic: Outer Joins and Finding Missing Data
subtopics: RIGHT JOIN and FULL OUTER JOIN
days.lab_task: Find customers who never ordered, products never sold, each employee with their manager's name, and order counts per customer including customers with zero orders.
days.deliverable: Outer join queries and results
checks: Count orders per customer including zero
Zero appears for customers with no orders
Move a filter from ON to WHERE in a LEFT JOIN

subtopics: NOT IN and the NULL trap
days.lab_task: Find products priced above the average, customers whose total spend is above their country's average, and customers with no orders using NOT EXISTS and NOT IN, explaining any difference.
days.deliverable: Subquery queries, results and the NOT IN explanation
checks: Use NOT IN when the subquery contains a NULL
Rewrite one subquery as a join
objectives: Avoid the NOT IN NULL trap

days.topic: Set Operations: UNION, INTERSECT and EXCEPT
subtopics: Performance of UNION versus UNION ALL
days.lab_task: Combine 2023 and 2024 order archives, find customers who ordered in both years, and find products in the price list that are missing from the stock table.
days.deliverable: Set operation queries and results
checks: Combine both archives with UNION ALL
Row count equals the sum of both tables
Customers in both years with INTERSECT
Products missing from stock with EXCEPT

subtopics: Choosing data types: integer, numeric, text, varchar, date, timestamp, boolean
ALTER TABLE to add and change columns
days.lab_task: Create tables for a small course booking system with suitable data types, identity keys and defaults, then add a column and change a type with ALTER TABLE.
days.deliverable: Table creation script and the final table definitions
checks: Insert a booking without a created date
Insert a NULL into a NOT NULL column
Store a price of 19.99 in numeric(10,2)

subtopics: FOREIGN KEY and ON DELETE options
Integrity rules in the database versus the application
days.lab_task: Add primary, foreign, unique and check constraints to the booking system, then try ten bad inserts and show each one being rejected with the constraint name.
days.deliverable: Constraint script and the ten error messages
checks: Book a course that does not exist

subtopics: Checking affected rows before changing data
days.lab_task: Load bookings from a staging table with INSERT ... SELECT, apply a 10 percent price rise to one category, delete cancelled bookings older than a year and confirm each change with RETURNING.
days.deliverable: Change scripts and before and after row counts
checks: Run SELECT with the same WHERE before the DELETE
Row count matches the delete count

days.lab_task: Write a seat booking that reduces available seats and inserts a booking in one transaction, force a failure halfway, show the rollback and use a savepoint to keep part of a batch.
days.deliverable: Transaction scripts and results
checks: Open a transaction and update a row, then update it from a second session

days.lab_task: Create a monthly sales view and a customer view that hides emails and phone numbers, then build two reports on top of the views.
days.deliverable: View definitions and reports
checks: Matches the earlier GROUP BY results
Select email from the customer view
objectives: Use views for reporting and hiding data

subtopics: Seeing whether an index is used with EXPLAIN
days.lab_task: Load one million orders, time a search by customer and date without an index, add a suitable composite index, and compare EXPLAIN output and timings.
days.deliverable: Timings and EXPLAIN output before and after
checks: Query is at least ten times faster

subtopics: First, second and third normal form
days.lab_task: Redesign a provided flat spreadsheet of course bookings into a normalised schema with an ER diagram, create the tables and migrate the data with INSERT ... SELECT.
days.deliverable: ER diagram, schema script and migration script
checks: Explain which normal form each change fixed

subtopics: Turning a question into a query
days.lab_task: Answer ten business questions from the sales manager, such as the share of revenue by category, repeat customer rate and the best month per country, and export the answers to CSV.
days.deliverable: Ten queries, CSV exports and a one-page summary
checks: File opens correctly in a spreadsheet

days.lab_task: Design and build a small sales database for a shop from provided CSV files, clean and load the data, add constraints and indexes, create report views and present answers to eight business questions.
days.deliverable: Schema script, load scripts, views, answers and a 10-minute presentation
checks: Row counts match the source files after cleaning
Insert an order for a customer that does not exist
objectives: Combine the beginner topics in one database

intermediate.summary: For people who write everyday SELECT, JOIN and GROUP BY queries. Covers window functions, CTEs and recursion, advanced aggregation, query plans and indexing, transactions and isolation, procedural SQL, JSON, data cleaning and analytics patterns.
prerequisites: Writes joins, subqueries and GROUP BY queries confidently
outcomes: Solve analytical problems with window functions and CTEs
Read query plans and choose indexes
Write stored procedures, functions and triggers
Handle concurrency, JSON data and data quality in SQL

subtopics: CTEs with INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE
Testing each step of a query
When a temporary table is better
days.lab_task: Rewrite a provided 80-line nested query into a sequence of named CTEs, check each step's result, and use a data-changing CTE to archive and delete old orders in one statement.
days.deliverable: Rewritten query, step results and archive script
checks: Compare the old and new query results
Rows moved to the archive and deleted from orders in one statement
Run each CTE on its own
Every step returns the expected rows

days.topic: Recursive Queries for Hierarchies and Graphs
days.lab_task: Use recursive queries to print the full management chain for every employee with depth, total the parts in a product's bill of materials and fill missing dates in a daily sales report.
days.deliverable: Recursive queries and results
checks: Show the chain for one employee
Lists every manager up to the CEO
Introduce a cycle in the data
Query stops and flags the cycle
Every day of the month appears with zero for missing days

days.lab_task: Rank products by revenue within each category, find the top three per category, split customers into spending quartiles and remove duplicate customer rows keeping the newest.
days.deliverable: Window queries and results
checks: Correct products with ties handled as specified
Remove duplicates keeping the newest row
Compare RANK and DENSE_RANK with ties
Participant explains the gap in RANK

days.topic: Window Functions: Running Totals and Comparisons
days.lab_task: Build a daily sales report with a running monthly total, a seven-day moving average, the change from the previous day and each day's share of the month.
days.deliverable: Report query and results
checks: Running total on the last day of the month
Seven-day moving average for a given day
Previous-day change on the first day
objectives: Compare rows with LAG and LEAD

days.topic: Advanced Aggregation: GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP and CUBE
days.lab_task: Produce a sales report with subtotals by country and category and a grand total, a pivot of revenue by month as columns, and median order value per country.
days.deliverable: Aggregation queries and results
checks: Pivot months into columns with FILTER

days.topic: Reading Query Plans with EXPLAIN ANALYZE
subtopics: Scan types: sequential, index, index-only, bitmap
Join types: nested loop, hash, merge
days.lab_task: Analyse the plans of five slow report queries, identify the costly step and the wrong row estimates in each, and write down the fix you would try.
days.deliverable: Annotated plans and proposed fixes
checks: Run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on a slow query
Find a large gap between estimated and actual rows
Name the join type used in each plan

days.lab_task: Use pg_stat_statements to find the five most expensive queries in a workload, design indexes for them including a partial and an expression index, and drop two unused indexes.
days.deliverable: Index changes, plans and workload timings before and after
checks: Run the workload before and after
Total time at least 50 percent lower
objectives: Use partial, covering and expression indexes

days.lab_task: Rewrite six slow queries from a provided application log so they can use indexes, replace OFFSET paging with keyset paging and update ten million rows in batches.
days.deliverable: Rewritten queries, plans and timings
checks: Rewrite WHERE date(created_at) = ... as a range

subtopics: Read committed, repeatable read and serializable
Dirty reads, non-repeatable reads and phantoms
Row locks and SELECT ... FOR UPDATE
days.lab_task: Reproduce a lost update with two sessions, fix it with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and with a version column, create and resolve a deadlock, and build a job queue with SKIP LOCKED.
days.deliverable: Session scripts, outputs and explanations
checks: Run two concurrent seat bookings without locking
Second waits and the result is correct
Run four workers on the SKIP LOCKED queue

days.lab_task: Write a function that returns a customer's order summary as a table and a procedure that places an order, checks stock, raises clear errors and commits in batches for bulk loads.
days.deliverable: Function and procedure code with test calls
checks: Place an order for more than the stock
Clear error raised and nothing changed

days.lab_task: Add an audit trigger that records who changed each price and when, a trigger that maintains updated_at and one that blocks deleting paid invoices.
days.deliverable: Trigger code, audit rows and test results
checks: Audit row holds old price, new price, user and time
Update 100,000 rows with and without the trigger

days.topic: Upserts and MERGE: Loading and Synchronising Data
subtopics: MERGE with matched and not matched actions
MERGE in SQL Server and Oracle
days.lab_task: Synchronise a product table from a daily supplier file loaded into a staging table, inserting new products, updating changed prices, soft-deleting missing ones and running the load twice with the same result.
days.deliverable: Load script, staging table and before and after counts
checks: Run the load on day-one data
New products inserted and counts match the file
Load day-two data with a removed product

subtopics: Staleness and when it is acceptable
days.lab_task: Replace a slow dashboard query with a materialised view refreshed every 15 minutes by pg_cron, refresh it concurrently while the dashboard is in use and document the staleness rule.
days.deliverable: View definition, refresh job and timing comparison
checks: Query the dashboard before and after
Response time drops from seconds to milliseconds
objectives: Speed up reports with materialised views

days.topic: Working with JSON and Semi-Structured Data
subtopics: Building JSON with json_build_object and json_agg
JSON in MySQL and SQL Server
days.lab_task: Load product events stored as JSON, extract fields into a report, index a frequently searched attribute and return API-ready JSON for each order with its lines.
days.deliverable: JSON queries, index and sample output
checks: Find events where payload->>'device' is mobile
Search a jsonb attribute with and without a GIN index
Build an order as nested JSON

days.topic: Data Cleaning and Quality Checks in SQL
days.lab_task: Clean a messy imported customer and orders dataset: remove duplicates, standardise country codes, validate emails, flag outliers and write reconciliation checks that must return zero rows.
days.deliverable: Cleaning scripts, rejected rows table and check queries
checks: Run the duplicate check after cleaning
Validate emails with a regular expression
Reconcile order totals with line totals

days.topic: Date, Time and Time Zone Handling
days.lab_task: Build a calendar table with fiscal periods and holidays, report orders by local day for three time zones, and find overlapping room bookings.
days.deliverable: Calendar table script and queries
checks: Report the same order in UTC and India time

days.topic: Analytical Patterns: Cohorts, Funnels and Retention
subtopics: Customer cohorts by first purchase month
days.lab_task: Build a monthly cohort retention table, a sign-up to purchase funnel from event data, sessions with a 30-minute gap rule and RFM segments for customers.
days.deliverable: Analytical queries and result tables
checks: Funnel conversion from sign-up to purchase
Split one user's events into sessions
Correct session count with the 30-minute rule

days.lab_task: Write Flyway migrations that add a required column to a large table without long locks: add it nullable, backfill in batches, add the constraint as NOT VALID then validate, and create an index concurrently.
days.deliverable: Migration files and lock monitoring output
checks: Run the migration while an application writes
No write waits longer than one second

days.lab_task: Create read-only, application and admin roles, restrict the application to its schema, add row-level security so each tenant sees only its rows and show SQL injection being stopped by parameters.
days.deliverable: Role scripts, policy definitions and test results
checks: Read another tenant's rows as the application role
Send an injection string through a parameterised query

days.topic: Intermediate Capstone: Analytics Database for an Online Store
days.lab_task: Build an analytics database for an online store with migrations, cleaned data, cohort and funnel views, tuned indexes, an audited order procedure and role-based access, then present the results.
days.deliverable: Migration repository, views, performance report and a 15-minute presentation
checks: Can read views but not raw customer emails
objectives: Combine the intermediate topics in one database

advanced.summary: For experienced SQL developers and database engineers. Covers optimiser internals, advanced tuning, partitioning, concurrency at scale, replication and high availability, warehouse modelling, advanced analytics, operations and moving between database engines.
prerequisites: Writes window functions, CTEs and procedural SQL
Reads query plans and designs indexes
Has run a production database or a large reporting database
outcomes: Tune queries using optimiser and statistics knowledge
Design partitioned, replicated and highly available databases
Model data warehouses and write advanced analytical SQL
Operate, secure and migrate databases at scale

subtopics: Forcing and hinting plans across engines
days.lab_task: Find a query where correlated columns cause a bad row estimate and a slow plan, fix it with extended statistics, and show the plan and timing change.
days.deliverable: Plans and statistics before and after with an explanation
checks: Compare estimated and actual rows before the fix
Estimate off by more than ten times
Estimate within two times of actual
objectives: Explain how the optimiser chooses plans

subtopics: Join strategies and when each wins
Tuning a whole workload, not one query
days.lab_task: Tune a provided reporting workload of twelve queries using plans, memory settings, lateral joins and rewrites until total runtime drops by at least 70 percent.
days.deliverable: Tuning log, plans and workload timings
checks: Find a sort spilling to disk
Spill removed by work_mem or a rewrite
Rewrite a correlated subquery with LATERAL

days.topic: Advanced Indexing: BRIN, GIN, GiST and Full-Text Search
subtopics: BRIN indexes for large append-only tables
Full-text search with tsvector and tsquery
days.lab_task: Add a BRIN index to a 100-million-row event table, full-text search with ranking on product descriptions, trigram fuzzy search for names and an exclusion constraint that blocks double bookings.
days.deliverable: Index definitions, sizes and query results
checks: BRIN is a small fraction of the size

subtopics: Partitioning in MySQL and SQL Server
days.lab_task: Partition a 200-million-row orders table by month with pg_partman, show pruning in plans, archive a year by detaching partitions and migrate the existing table with minimal downtime.
days.deliverable: Partitioning scripts, plans and migration log
checks: Insert data for a future month
Lands in the right pre-created partition

days.topic: Concurrency at Scale: MVCC, Vacuum and Bloat
days.lab_task: Create bloat with heavy updates and a long-running transaction, measure it, tune autovacuum and fillfactor for the table and show bloat staying under control.
days.deliverable: Bloat measurements, settings and monitoring queries
checks: Hold a long transaction during updates
Dead rows are not cleaned until it ends
Dead tuple ratio stays under 10 percent

days.topic: Advanced Transaction Design and Serializable Isolation
subtopics: Two-phase commit and why to avoid it
days.lab_task: Reproduce write skew in an on-call rota under repeatable read, prevent it with serializable isolation and retries, then build an outbox table for reliable event publishing.
days.deliverable: Session scripts, retry code and outbox design
checks: Run two concurrent rota changes under repeatable read
Both commit and the rule is broken
One fails and succeeds on retry, rule kept
Event is still in the outbox and published later

subtopics: Connection routing with PgBouncer and HAProxy
Managed services: RDS, Azure Database, Cloud SQL
days.lab_task: Build a three-node Patroni cluster, route reads to replicas, measure replication lag under load, fail the primary during writes and show automatic failover.
days.deliverable: Cluster configuration, failover log and lag measurements

subtopics: Recovery time and recovery point objectives
days.lab_task: Set up pgBackRest with WAL archiving, drop a table by mistake, restore the database to one minute before the drop and measure recovery time.
days.deliverable: Backup configuration, recovery log and timing
checks: Restore to one minute before the drop
Table and its rows are back
Restore a pg_dump into a new database
objectives: Recover to a point in time

days.topic: Data Warehouse Modelling: Star Schemas and Slowly Changing Dimensions
days.lab_task: Design a star schema for store sales, load it from the operational database with a type 2 customer dimension, and answer reporting questions that need historic customer attributes.
days.deliverable: Dimensional model, load scripts and report queries
checks: Change a customer's city and reload
New dimension row with valid dates; old sales keep the old city
Total sales from the fact table
State the grain of the fact table

days.topic: ELT Pipelines in SQL with dbt
days.lab_task: Build the warehouse transformations as a dbt project with staging and mart models, an incremental fact model, snapshots and tests, and run it in CI on every pull request.
days.deliverable: dbt project, test results and lineage graph
checks: Insert a duplicate key in staging
Second run processes only new rows

days.lab_task: Find products frequently bought together, detect streaks of daily activity per user, compute the correlation between discount and quantity, and build a moving-average baseline forecast.
days.deliverable: Analytical queries and a findings summary
checks: Longest daily streak for a test user

subtopics: Cost models: scanned bytes and compute
days.lab_task: Run the same analytical queries on PostgreSQL and DuckDB locally and on one cloud warehouse, add clustering, compare time and scanned bytes and estimate monthly cost.
days.deliverable: Query results, timings, scanned bytes and cost estimate
checks: Run the report on PostgreSQL and DuckDB
DuckDB is clearly faster on the large scan
Add clustering on date in the warehouse
Scanned bytes drop for date filters
Based on measured bytes and frequency

days.topic: Geospatial, Graph and Vector Queries in SQL
days.lab_task: Find the stores within 5 km of each customer with PostGIS, compute the shortest delivery route with pgRouting, and run a similar-product search with pgvector filtered by category and stock.
days.deliverable: Queries, indexes and timing results
checks: Find stores within 5 km of a test customer
Run the vector search with an HNSW index
Returns the top 10 similar products in under 50 ms
Matches the expected path and distance

days.lab_task: Build a database dashboard for queries, waits, locks, connections, replication lag and cache hit ratio, then use it to diagnose a blocking chain injected during a load test.
days.deliverable: Dashboard export, alert rules and diagnosis notes

subtopics: Encryption at rest and in transit
Compliance requirements: GDPR and PCI DSS
days.lab_task: Encrypt card tokens with pgcrypto, mask personal data in a copy for testing, log access to sensitive tables with pgaudit and handle a customer deletion request across all tables.
days.deliverable: Security scripts, audit logs and deletion procedure
checks: Access is recorded in the audit log
Run the deletion procedure for one customer
No personal data remains in any table

subtopics: Shared table, schema per tenant and database per tenant
days.lab_task: Implement a shared-table multi-tenant schema with row-level security, distribute it across nodes with Citus by tenant, and move a large tenant to its own node.
days.deliverable: Schema, distribution configuration and tenant move log
checks: Completes with the tenant's data intact

subtopics: Differences between Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL and PostgreSQL
Migration tools: ora2pg, pgloader, AWS DMS
Change data capture for low-downtime moves
days.lab_task: Migrate a MySQL database with data and stored routines to PostgreSQL using pgloader, convert two procedures by hand, validate data with counts and checksums and write a cutover plan.
days.deliverable: Migration scripts, validation report and cutover plan
checks: Compare row counts for every table
Checksums are identical on both engines

days.topic: SQL in Applications: ORMs, Pooling and Performance
subtopics: Batching and bulk loading with COPY
Timeouts at the database and application
days.lab_task: Find N+1 queries in a provided application from the database logs, fix them, put PgBouncer in front of the database, bulk-load with COPY and set statement timeouts.
days.deliverable: Fixes, pooling configuration and before and after metrics
checks: Load the order page before and after the fix
Queries per page drop from 51 to 2
Database connections stay under the pool size
Run a query longer than the statement timeout

subtopics: Sudden slow queries after a release
days.lab_task: Work through four injected incidents (a plan regression, a lock storm, WAL filling the disk and connection exhaustion), restore service, find root causes and write runbooks.
days.deliverable: Incident timelines, fixes and runbooks
checks: Restore normal query times after the plan regression
Free disk space from WAL growth
Cause found and disk usage falls
Write a runbook for the lock storm

days.topic: Advanced Capstone: Production Data Platform Design
subtopics: Operational schema with partitioning and security
Failure drill, presentation and design defence
days.lab_task: Design and build a data platform with a partitioned, secured operational database, a highly available cluster with tested point-in-time recovery, a dbt warehouse and monitoring, then run a failure drill and present it.
days.deliverable: Design document, scripts, dbt project, dashboards, drill report and a 20-minute presentation
checks: Fail the primary during the drill
Failover completes and no committed data is lost
Restore to a point in time
Run the warehouse build and the report workload
Tests pass and reports meet the speed targets
objectives: Combine the advanced topics in one platform
